comments: This is a Rāgmala depiction of Vasant Ragini. There are 4 musicians one of them is playing the Pakhawaj one is playing the Manjira and one is playing the Been. The other two musicians are clapping their hands.

A painting of Maharana Ari Singh with his courtiers being entertained at the Jagniwas Water Palace. There is one musician playing the Pakhawaj. The foreground shows a set of dancers accompanied by musicians playing sārangi and tablā. The pakhāwaj player is depicted in the lower part of the painting.

A painting of Maharaja Bijay Singh in his harem. There are two musicians one is playing the Pakhawaj and the other is playing the Been. The musician playing the Been is depicted in the lower part of the painting.
Yet another Rāgmala depiction of Vasant Ragini. There are two musicians one is playing the pakhāwaj and the other is playing the Manjirā.

A rāgmala depiction of Shri Raga. There are 2 musicians playing Vīṇā. Though both Vīṇā are of different types. The musician on the right of the viewer is playing a vīṇā with a single gourd resonator while the other one is playing a vīṇā with two gourd resonators.
Probably one of the earliest depiction of a protoinstrument of pakhāwaj player in Indian miniature painting. The musician on the left of the viewer is seen playing the pakhāwaj.
Here the tuning pastes are visible on both the drumheads of the pakhāwaj.
